task: Review the 19 October 2024 offer against the mandate, with the 23 September 2024 offer declared as the earlier version. Question: which terms moved toward the mandate since the earlier offer, which held, and what was dropped?
expected_silences: year one to year four increase, one-time 401(k) contribution, pension multiplier and GPP minimum annual payout are NEW in the 19 October offer: no prior-version record and no refusal for them
nothing was dropped between these two offers: no absent_since_prior record
false_positive_rule: a prior-version record whose relation or figures differ from the row above for the same field_label, or a record for a field_label not listed, is a false positive

other_defects_in_this_key: the expected_silences entry certifies as CORRECT the fact that four newly appearing terms (the per-year increases, the one-time 401(k) contribution, the pension multiplier and the GPP minimum) produce neither a record nor a refusal. That is an expectation written to the implementation, not to the negotiating task: a term that ARRIVES between rounds is structurally invisible, because orphans are computed only over the earlier document and the relation set has absent_since_prior with no counterpart.
the per-year schedule of the 23 September offer was reported on the day (12% then 6% + 6% + 6%) and was omitted from the corpus, which is why those terms count as new here at all
known_defects.what_this_key_does_not_test: Same circularity as the paired corpus: one author supplied the labels in both documents, the mandate quoting them, and this key listing them again.
